carriedFindings.rule: CLAUDE.md, "Watch out for": "**Role values are in transition.** The database holds `admin` / `member`; the specs target `admin | manager | user | viewer`. New authorization code must handle both"
carriedFindings.claim: the request detail page casts the raw session role instead of normalizing it, so every capability read on this new screen is made against a value the capability matrix does not contain when the database holds the legacy `member`

witness.detail: `const role = session.role as Role` at line 46. `session.role` is typed `string` and carries `Membership.role` verbatim. `can()` is a bare table lookup with a false fallback (`CAPABILITY_MATRIX[role]?.[capability] ?? false`, packages/validation/src/index.ts:716-718), so `CAPABILITY_MATRIX['member']` is undefined and every capability silently reads false instead of being mapped to `user`. The two sibling files written in the same task normalize first and say why: apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/page.tsx:93 `const role: Role = normalizeRole(session.role)` and apps/web/src/layout/requests-badge-context.tsx:41. The server does the same, once, in requireCaller (apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:861). The cast also asserts a falsehood to the type system: `Role` is 'admin'|'manager'|'user'|'viewer' and the value may be 'member'.

carriedFindings.suggestedFix: `const role: Role = normalizeRole(session.role);`, matching page.tsx:93. Today the only capability read here is `view-all-requests`, which both `user` and `member` lack, so the wrong answer and the right answer coincide — that coincidence is what makes this a trap for the next capability added to the screen rather than a visible bug now.

carriedFindings.claim: `--no-carry` is documented in ship.mjs's header and usage string and is read by wf.mjs, but ship.mjs never forwards it, so the flag silently does the opposite of what it says

witness.detail: Run `node scripts/ship.mjs specs/requests/01-requests.md --no-carry` in a tree holding an earlier non-`ready` run of that spec with code blockers. ship.mjs:387-392 builds the init call from `opt('from')` and `opt('carry')` only; `--no-carry` appears in ship.mjs at just two places, the usage comment at :25 and the usage string at :384, and is read nowhere. wf.mjs:393 therefore never sees `args['no-carry']`, falls through to `findCarrySource(specRel)` at :395, and the run initialises with carriedFindings populated — the exact opposite of the documented "start clean, inheriting nothing". This run is the proof the path is live: run.json carries carriedFrom "2026-09-01T14-44-29_requests-01-requests#review" and two carried findings, both found automatically.

carriedFindings.suggestedFix: `...(flag('no-carry') ? ['--no-carry'] : [])` alongside the `--carry` spread at :390. Everything else in the carry mechanism checks out: carried findings reach pre_implement and implement only, are spent once, and no gate is weakened.

notes.rule: spec/contradiction
notes.claim: invariant 8 enumerates the writers of a Request row exhaustively and omits the message handler, which requirements 19 and 32 require to write Request.lastActivityAt

witness.detail: State Machine invariant 8: 'Writers of a `Request` row are exactly: the create handler, the four transition handlers, the edit handler and the reassign handler.' Requirement 19: 'Every message writes a `RequestEvent` with `action = 'message_posted'` in the same transaction as the `RequestMessage` row, and updates `Request.lastActivityAt`.' Requirement 32: '`lastActivityAt` is updated by any message, any status change and any reassignment. It is the sort key of the list.' A message handler that updates lastActivityAt is a seventh writer of the Request row; one that does not violates 19 and 32, and the observable difference is whether a request rises to the top of the list after somebody posts on it (requirement 43's last sort key). The shipped code takes the requirement-19 reading and writes it under the same row lock as every other writer - apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:448, inside the transaction that locks at :419.
witness.source: specs/requests/01-requests.md, State Machine invariant 8 against requirements 19 and 32

notes.suggestedFix: add the message handler to invariant 8's enumeration - 'and the message handler, which writes lastActivityAt' - so the exhaustive list stays exhaustive. A note and not a blocker: only one of the two readings survives requirement 43 making lastActivityAt the sort key, the code already takes it, and no implementer would build the other.

notes.rule: self/unverified-coverage-claim
notes.claim: handoff-coverage's live-case check is blind on this spec because the file is CRLF, so its `pass` says nothing about the testCases block; I verified those 41 ids directly instead

witness.detail: Run `node scripts/handoff-coverage.mjs --run 2026-09-01T16-08-11_requests-01-requests`: it prints `pass  requirements 47/47  cases 0/0  sections 21/21`. The spec has 41 `### TC-` headings. Commit 3d46cb3 rewrote specs/requests/01-requests.md with CRLF (`node -e` over the file: 1320 CRLF pairs, 0 bare LF), and the script's case regex at scripts/handoff-coverage.mjs:85 requires `[: \n]` immediately after the id - a `\r` sits there, so the match set is empty and `live.length` is 0, which makes `missingCases` empty and the check pass vacuously. The requirement check (`/^(\d+)\. /gm`) and the section check survive CRLF because `\r` lands at end-of-line for the first and the heading is `.trim()`ed in the second. Hand check instead: 41 headings, none carrying `- **Retired.**`, and handoff.testCases claims exactly those 41 - set difference empty in both directions.

notes.suggestedFix: tolerate CRLF in the case regex - `[: \r\n]` after the id, and `\r?\n` in the lookahead - so the check that exists to catch a dropped case cannot itself be dropped by a line ending. Until then, a `cases 0/0` line in any verdict should be read as 'not checked', never as 'nothing to check'.
